messages.author: 1760854b2bf7b077
messages.subject: STAR output to featureCount-resorting
parts:
Hi Subread team,

 I really like this awesome tool, especially the fast performance of featureCount. I recently need to process a lot of samples using STAR aligner, then count read by featureCount. But the problem I got is: no matter I set "--outSAMtype BAM Unsorted" or "--outSAMtype BAM SortedByCoordinate" in STAR, featureCount always re-sort the bam. I read this thread about the incompatibility of STAR/samtools sort. Just wondering if there are any changes in the new version? I guess I can use "−−donotsort " on STAR sorted bam files? How is the accuracy? 

 Many thanks!

Ji

messages.author: bce99ba71cd48eea
messages.subject: Re: STAR output to featureCount-resorting
parts:
Hi Ji,

I ran STAR (v2.6.0c) on the "BAM Unsorted" mode to map a paired-end sample, then used featureCounts (v1.6.2) on the mapping results. No "reads from the same pair were found not adjacent" message was reported. 

I then ran STAR on the "BAM SortedByCoordinate" mode to map the same paired-end sample, and featureCounts reported the "reads from the same pair were found not adjacent" message. 

Can you please provide us with your full command line for running STAR and featureCounts?

BTW, the read counting results are identical in the above two runs. 

Cheers,
Yang

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: STAR output to featureCount-resorting
parts: You should not use the "−−donotsort" option unless you are absolutely sure that both reads from a pair are present in your bam file and they are next to each other in the bam file. If this is not the case, reads from different pairs might be treated as being from the same pair and then incorrectly counted.

messages.author: 1760854b2bf7b077
messages.subject: Re: STAR output to featureCount-resorting
parts:
Hi, 

 As suggested by Yang, I upgraded to featureCount v1.6.3 (from v1.5.1) and problem solved. I post here, just to keep a record in case others encounter the same problem.

 Thank you.

Ji
